title: Pager: recommendation-service p95 and memory both off baseline (Mar 2025)
symptoms: errors appearing late in the window after a long slow period
occasional allocation failures or container restarts late in the incident
process memory usage climbing for tens of minutes
latency growing in step with memory, not with a sudden traffic spike
timeouts that could be mistaken for a slow dependency
observed_signals: CPU increased only moderately until GC became frequent
latency correlated with memory; errors arrived later
memory_usage rose smoothly over a long period rather than in a single jump

timeline.event: a deploy or flag change on recommendation-service that populated a new cache
memory_usage on recommendation-service began a near-linear climb
GC / heap warnings became frequent on recommendation-service
a second climb started until the code fix landed

contributing_factors: an in-process cache had no eviction policy
the growth was slow enough that a 15-minute baseline looked almost normal at first
resolution: restarted the affected deployment as immediate mitigation
identified an unbounded in-process cache with no TTL
shipped a hotfix with eviction and a heap-growth alert
lessons_learned: caches without TTL belong on the review checklist for every service
a restart that restores latency is mitigation, not a fix
